title: Breaker loop between request coalescer and scheduler causing short-session TTFT sag
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: Over the last 48 hours multiple customers reported sudden TTFT (time-to-first-token) and tokens/sec degradation for short sessions (<128 tokens) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters. Investigation shows the regression began after the coalescer window adjustment shipped in runtime-1.23.2 (coalesce_window_ms: 2 -> 8). Root cause hypothesis: increased coalescer batching introduced a feedback loop with the scheduler's preemption/backpressure heuristic, creating bursty queueing & starvation for low-latency short requests. Impact: median TTFT for short sessions rose from ~80ms to ~360ms; some enterprise Private clusters observed 2-3x token/sec drop and customer escalations from EU customers CUST-4412 and CUST-4419. This ticket tracks triage, hotfix, and follow-ups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy runtime-1.23.2 with coalesce_window_ms=8 to a small cluster (or use hosted-canary).
2) Fire a mix of short single-turn requests (<=128 tokens) at 200 rps together with several long-context streams (>=1024 tokens) to simulate heterogenous fanout.
3) Observe surge in first-token latency for short requests and drop in tokens/sec using /metrics (prometheus) query: increase in runtime_queue_length and scheduler_preempt_count.
4) Revert coalesce_window_ms to 2 and re-run to observe TTFT reduction back to baseline.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC first pager from Customer Success (CUST-4412). 2026-03-11: NAT logs and Prom queries show correlation between coalescer window change and growing scheduler preempt rate. Heap snapshots show increased inflight KV cache holds during coalesced batches. Profiling indicates that coalesced microbatches hold GPU execution slots longer, triggering scheduler to raise preemption aggressiveness which then starves short sessions waiting in separate queues. Notable metrics: short_session_ttft_p50 from 82ms->360ms; scheduler_preempt_count +420% in 6h. Private clusters with constrained CPU for router had worst impact.
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): revert coalesce_window_ms to 2 in runtime-1.23.2 rollout (canary -> staged) and add a temporary per-tenant coalescer cap for enterprise clusters. Medium-term: implement adaptive coalescer that respects request priority and per-model session length distribution, plus a backpressure circuit breaker in the scheduler that prevents preemption oscillations. Add automated canary checks for short-session TTFT regressions. Rollout strategy: 1) canary revert in hosted canary (10% traffic), 2) monitor 2h, 3) staged rollback to Dedicated & Private, 4) patch release runtime-1.23.3 with fix and QA.
current_status: Canary revert patch deployed to hosted-canary at 2026-03-15 04:40 UTC (runtime-1.23.2-revert-coalescer). Initial metrics: short_session_ttft_p50 reduced from ~360ms -> ~95ms in canary. Monitoring alerts suppressed but keeping high-sensitivity alarms enabled. Dedicated/Private rollouts pending PM approval due to customer impact and upgrade windows.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Reverting coalescer window reduces batching efficiency for long-context requests and may increase cost; however customer SLA and immediate latency regressions make revert necessary. Longer-term adaptive solution requires more testing; risk of reintroducing throughput regressions if adaptive heuristics are too aggressive. Private clusters with customized router CPU profiles may need operator-assisted upgrades.
